blocks.heading: Government objectives
blocks.text: Governments pursue economic objectives such as employment, sustainable growth, price stability and a sustainable external economic position, alongside social aims such as improved living standards, fair opportunity, access to essential services and environmental protection. Objectives can conflict: a project creating employment may also damage a shared environment, while protection costs can limit some commercial activity. A business’s profit objective does not by itself show whether these wider aims are achieved. State the relevant outcome and parties rather than assume any increase in business output benefits everyone equally.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A local project would create employment but also create dust near homes. Employment supports an economic and social aim, while environmental protection requires attention to residents’ separate costs. Both consequences belong in the decision.
